item.group_name: Image edits (the user brings a picture)

expect.asks_about: Whether cleanup means removing countertop clutter or changing the kitchen's appearance.

item.title: Clean Up This Kitchen
item.tests: Tests conservative interpretation of a vague cleanup request, clearing clutter without inventing a renovation.

answer_sheet.Meaning of cleanup: Clear the loose clutter off the counter, not a renovation.
answer_sheet.Permanent kitchen features: Keep the brown cabinets, beige tiles, counter material and existing kitchen layout.
answer_sheet.Style and size: Keep it a realistic photo with the same wide framing; free-tier resolution is fine.

must_haves: The countertop looks visibly tidier, with loose clutter removed.
The original brown wooden cabinets and beige tiles remain, rather than being replaced with renovated finishes.
The kitchen layout, fixed fixtures and viewpoint match the source.
Cleared counter areas look continuous and natural, without obvious erasure marks or floating object remnants.

turns.text: Can you clean up this kitchen pic by clearing the loose clutter off the counter, rather than doing a renovation? I keep getting distracted by the mess when I look at it, so I’d love to see it tidied up. You can decide which loose items to remove, but please keep the brown cabinets, beige tiles, counter material and existing kitchen layout as they are. I just mean a cleanup of what’s sitting out, with the image staying a realistic photo in the same wide framing. Free-tier resolution is fine.
turns.agent:
I couldn't make the cleaned-up image. Magic Hour turned down the edit because your account doesn't have enough credits, so nothing was created and there's no download link.

I'd already tried the cheapest setup your free plan allows: the flux-2-klein editing model at 640px, making one image (about 5 credits). There's no cheaper way to run this edit.

**To get it working:** add credits to your Magic Hour account by buying a credit pack or waiting for your free credits to refill. Then let me know and I'll run the same edit again.

**The edit I tried:**
- **Removed from the counters:** the can and knife, the plastic bag, the white bowl, the yellow container and glass cutting board on the left. Also the cloths and sponges by the main sink, the red and green mugs, the white canister and paper towel roll, the bowls and blue cup on the right, and the plate, sponge and bag in the second sink. The counter stains would be cleaned up too.
- **Kept:** the brown cabinets, beige tiles, outlets, counter material, both sinks and taps, the window, the layout, the lighting and the same wide view. I left the white kettle out because it looks like it belongs there. I can remove it too if you'd like.

style.prompt: Tidy up this kitchen photo by removing only the loose clutter. Remove: the can and the knife on the left counter, the plastic bag, white bowl, yellow container and the glass cutting board on the left counter, the cloths/sponges and dark items around the main sink, the red and green mugs, the white canister, the paper towel roll, the bowls, blue cup and small items on the right counter, the plate, sponge and plastic bag in the right sink, and the towel hanging on the white cabinet. Keep the white electric kettle. Leave the countertops clean and empty, wiped clean of stains. Keep everything else exactly the same: the brown wooden cabinets and their handles, the beige wall tiles, the outlets, the same countertop material and color, both sinks and faucets, the white unit, the window, the kitchen layout, lighting, camera angle and wide framing. Photorealistic, same photo, no renovation, no new objects.

I'm weighing whether to drop the kettle too, since it's an appliance and could go either way. I'll lean toward removing the loose clutter and keeping the kettle for realism.
